questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I study German, so Berlin was obvious for me language wise. I have been to Berlin many times, and I love the city. I also didn't want to go to far away, as that would be too expensive and at the time I didn't want to leave too far from friends and family.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think most of the information was fairly easy to find, but there was a lot of it, and it cut have been put all into one place, instead of being so many emails and websites.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Freie Uni was very organised and very good at creating social activities for exchange students. That was amazing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My family owns an apartment in Berlin, so for me very easy. For everyone else I met in Berlin, it sounded like a nightmare to find housing. The student housing was so far out from the city, very sad.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try and stay in the southern areas of Berlin, to get the maximum Berlin city experience and only 30 minute public transport to Freie. I reccomend Wilmersdorf, Schöneberg and Kreuzberg could work too.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to show up at campus to print my campus ID and then activate it at campus as well. I payed small tuition fee online. I dont remember other steps.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could email the office or show up at help desk at campus

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. I got all the classes i wanted and needed. This is because of the great professors at Freie, who manage to fit you in, even if the course is full. Just email them, they are so nice.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If in doubt, email the office right away, they take some time to reply. The other exchange students are also a big help, some of them have already taken a semester at Freie before you, so they know how to do it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great course list! So many options. I loved the courses that were made specifically for exchange students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was similar to the level at KU in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers at FU were very pedagogical and educational. Very helpful. The classes i took were max. 30 people and everyone got a chance to either say something or not to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Migration und Religion, Saviour of Humankind, Power and Welfare, Das Kreative Berlin and Integration in Germany.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all of my courses. My favorites were Integration in Germany and Saviour of Humankind.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Only the tuition fee at Freie. But that included pupblic transport all overberlin for 6 months, so i guess not that unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Entrance fee at nightclubs was a bit expensive, but thats it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different sports, including horsebackriding, volleyball, yoga etc. So many cool and cheap activities such as going to see Herthas game at Olympia stadion for 3 euro

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definetly keep an eye on international student club, add them to you email list. They do nice cheap activities alle the time.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Experience Berlin clubs, go to museums on sundays (its free the first sunday of the month), go to the many parks, go out to eat, go to Krumme Lanke lake

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get out there on the first days you meet all of the other exchange students. Everyone who shows up for the social activities at Freie are all seeking friends! Get poeple's whatsapp and instagram and just invite yourself to plans!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The only cultural difference I experienced was that the professors expect to be called by last name. And they call us by last name as well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Berlin night life

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try and engage in some German speaking activities (or else you will be speaking english all the time and not learn any german)
Sign up for a sport!
Live together with someone, dont live alone

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not reccomend biking in Berlin. Copenhagen bike lane standards are so much better, and you will get frustrated biking in Berlin. Instead just walk, or take public transport thats included in tuition fee. Or Uber is also so cheap.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not being shy, and forcing myself to make friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
